# General staff and war college (`general_staff_war_college`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/military.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Warfare, security & deterrence (`military`)
- Deps: needs standing_army_logistics; helped by strategy_theory, railway, electric_telegraph, map_projection_charts, wargaming_operations_research
- Core idea: A permanent body of specially selected and schooled officers that, in peacetime, maps the theatres of war, studies past campaigns, prepares mobilisation and transport plans and tests them in map exercises and staff rides. In war each commander gets a trained chief of staff who shares his responsibility, so that the army does not depend on one genius. Orders state the aim and leave the method to the man on the spot. Selection is by examination, not birth, and honest criticism after every exercise and war is a duty.
- Pitfalls:
  - A staff is not the commander's clerks and couriers; its core is planning and independent judgement
  - Plans do not survive contact with the enemy (Moltke); the staff's product is officers who can improvise to a common doctrine
  - A staff that answers to no civilian authority makes policy by its plans, as the German mobilisation schedule did in 1914
  - Promotion by seniority or purchase defeats the purpose
- History: china: 702 – Tang military examinations; 1080 – Song military academy curriculum fixed on the Seven Military Classics; europe: 1796 – Berthier's staff for Napoleon; 1807–1814 – Scharnhorst and Gneisenau create the Prussian General Staff; 1810 – Berlin war school (later Kriegsakademie); 1857–1888 – Moltke, railway mobilisation, victories of 1866 and 1870; east_asia: 1878 – Japanese general staff on the Prussian model; americas: 1884 – US Naval War College; 1903 – US Army general staff
- Read:
  - Walter Goerlitz, History of the German General Staff 1657–1945 (1953)
  - Trevor N. Dupuy, A Genius for War: The German Army and General Staff 1807–1945 (1977)
